summary: The paper poses live-deployment sycophancy auditing as a ground-truth-free behavioral classification problem and tests the idea entirely inside a hand-built stochastic simulator: eight interaction-observable features (confidence trajectory, hedging, response-length dynamics) are generated with literature-directed effect directions but arbitrary magnitudes, four of which are constructed with an additive offset proportional to the ground-truth label. A random forest trained on these features reaches 0.97 AUC / 0.95 F1 on the simulated changed-answer subset, a coefficient-attenuation sweep shows this degrading smoothly to chance as the injected effect is removed, and a downstream policy simulation shows gating reversion on the classifier beats both 'always trust' and 'revert on any change' baselines. This revision's specific contribution is closing a gap the paper says four prior reviewers converged on: the 5-seed feature-rank-stability check and the real-data network probe are now implemented as code in the shipped experiment.py/network_probe.py rather than only narrated in prose.
strengths:
- I ran experiment.py fresh and every headline number in the paper reproduces exactly: RF AUC 0.9742/F1 0.9519 (paper: 0.974/0.952), n=3847 (paper: n≈3850), 10-seed AUC mean 0.9766±0.0046 (paper: 0.977±0.005), smart-audit policy 93.1% single-seed / 93.5±0.9% 10-seed mean (paper: 93.1%/93.5±0.9%), and the effect_scale sweep (0.506, 0.593, 0.722, 0.845, 0.941, 0.974 vs. paper's 0.506/0.593/0.722/0.845/0.941/0.974) — a genuinely rare level of exact match between a paper's tables and a from-scratch re-run.
- The specific gap the paper claims to fix is actually fixed: the feature_rank_stability block exists in experiment.py, running it reproduces hedge_latency as the top feature in all 5 seeds with importances matching the reported ranges (0.376-0.416), and network_probe.py exists and, when read, produces exactly the exception text quoted in Sec 3.6 (RuntimeError: 'Cannot send a request, as the client has been closed', and the identical CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED text across three hosts) — this is not a paraphrase, the log file matches verbatim.
- The paper is unusually disciplined about its own limitations: it states plainly that 4/8 features are constructed with a label-proportional offset (so high AUC is partly true by construction), that the effect_scale mid-range is 'illustrative only', and gives concrete, falsifiable criteria (AUC near 0.50 on real data, or importance concentrating on a labeling artifact) for when the audit-logic claim should be considered wrong.
weaknesses:
- The core empirical result is still a classifier recovering a signal that the authors themselves injected into the data (four features get an additive offset proportional to the very label being predicted); this is acknowledged in Limitations, but it means the paper's central AUC/F1/accuracy numbers say very little about detectability in real transcripts, and the paper does not offer any way to translate the effect_scale sensitivity curve into a real-world estimate other than reporting that one doesn't exist.
- No real interaction data, model, or human transcripts are used anywhere; the single external validation attempt (Sec 3.6) fails at the network layer before any real data is touched, so the 'this transfers to live deployment monitoring' framing in the introduction is aspirational rather than demonstrated, and remains so after this revision.
- The related-work section is honest that no prior work supplies calibrated micro-signature coefficients, but this also means there is no empirical anchor at all for the chosen effect magnitudes — an ablation grounding at least one feature (e.g., hedge_latency, which the paper itself says is capturable from existing production logging) against any real-world proxy, even a small pilot, would have substantially strengthened the claim; the paper explicitly declines to do this ('We did not do this in the time available').
questions:
1. Given that hedge_latency is described as already present in most production LLM logs, was a quick pilot (even the 10-20 hand-timed transcripts the paper mentions as a next step) truly infeasible within the revision window, or was it deprioritized in favor of the code-provenance fixes?
2. The paper says the first-draft hedge_count-led feature ranking cannot be reconstructed or explained; does this affect confidence in any other unlisted design choices in simulate_dataset() (e.g., the specific Beta/Uniform/Normal parameters), or is hedge_latency's dominance robust to reasonable perturbations of those choices beyond the effect_scale sweep already reported?
3. For the base-rate sweep (Sec 3.4), AUC is stable within 0.01 across task accuracy 0.30-0.90, but this is still all conditioned on the same fixed feature-generation coefficients — would the ranking of feature importances also stay stable across that base-rate range, or only the aggregate AUC?
